paragraphs.title: The Heading and the Plea for Refuge

easy.explanation: The heading identifies it as a psalm of David.
easy.q: To whom is this psalm attributed in its heading?

easy.explanation: The heading says that David fled from Saul.
easy.q: From whom was David fleeing according to the heading?

easy.explanation: The heading places David in a cave.
easy.q: Where was David when this psalm was written?

medium.explanation: He repeatedly says, “Be merciful unto me, O God.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do at the beginning?

answers: Until his enemies leave the land
medium.explanation: He seeks refuge “until these calamities be overpast.”
medium.q: Until when does the psalmist seek refuge under God’s wings?

medium.explanation: The image describes trusting God for shelter and protection.
medium.q: What does making refuge in the shadow of God’s wings mean?

challenge.explanation: David faces calamity but trusts in refuge under God’s wings.
challenge.q: What contrast is central to the opening passage?

challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the intensity of David’s request for mercy.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “be merciful unto me” emphasize?

answers: It presents David in a situation of danger
challenge.explanation: David’s flight from Saul and his hiding in a cave explain his need for refuge.
challenge.q: How does the heading help explain the plea for refuge?

paragraphs.title: Hope for Rescue and Divine Kindness

easy.explanation: The verse says, “I will cry unto God most high.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist cry?

easy.explanation: God is asked to send help from heaven and save him.
easy.q: What does the psalmist expect God to send from heaven?

easy.explanation: The passage says that God sends forth His mercy and His truth.
easy.q: Which two qualities of God are mentioned at the end of the passage?

answers: He expects God to rescue him
He wants to describe the cave
He wants to begin a celebration
medium.explanation: He calls upon God because he trusts Him to save him.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist call upon God most high?

answers: God’s rescue reflects His faithful character
medium.explanation: The psalmist expects salvation because God is merciful and true.
medium.q: What relationship is shown between rescue and God’s mercy and truth?

answers: God completes and acts on the psalmist’s behalf
God speaks only to the nations
medium.explanation: The expression presents God as the one who carries out His purposes for the psalmist.
medium.q: In this context, what does “performeth all things for me” mean?

answers: That his rescue will be accomplished
That his enemies will disappear into the sky
challenge.explanation: He appeals to the God who performs all things for him and asks to be saved.
challenge.q: What expectation does the psalmist express in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The request shows that the psalmist expects God to intervene and rescue him.
challenge.q: What does the movement from crying to God to help from heaven show?

challenge.explanation: God’s mercy and truth are presented as the basis for hope.
challenge.q: Which qualities strengthen the psalmist’s confidence in rescue?

paragraphs.title: The Enemies and the Reversal of the Trap

easy.explanation: He says, “My soul is among lions.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say his soul is among?

answers: Spears, arrows, and a sharp sword
easy.explanation: Their teeth are called spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
easy.q: What images describe the enemies’ weapons and speech?

easy.explanation: They prepared a net and dug a pit before him.
easy.q: What did the enemies prepare for the psalmist’s steps?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “their tongue a sharp sword.”
medium.q: How is the enemies’ tongue described?

answers: The enemies fall into it themselves
medium.explanation: The enemies fall into the pit they dug.
medium.q: What eventually happens in the pit prepared by the enemies?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the psalmist’s low and distressed condition.
medium.q: What does “my soul is bowed down” communicate?

answers: The sword becomes a musical instrument
challenge.explanation: Those who prepared the pit fall into it themselves.
challenge.q: What is the central reversal in these verses?

answers: As dangerous in both action and speech
challenge.explanation: The images portray both physical violence and destructive speech.
challenge.q: How do the images of teeth, arrows, and a sword portray the enemies?

answers: The evil they planned returns upon them
challenge.explanation: The verse depicts the reversal of the enemies’ plot against themselves.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the enemies’ falling into their own pit?

paragraphs.title: A Heart Ready for Song and Praise

easy.q: What does the psalmist say about his heart?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will sing and give praise.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist intend to do?

easy.explanation: The verse names the psaltery and harp.

answers: He prepares his heart to sing
medium.explanation: He declares that his heart is fixed and ready for praise.
medium.q: What does the psalmist do after describing danger?

medium.explanation: He says, “I myself will awake early.”
medium.q: When does the psalmist say he will awake?

answers: A call to awaken for praise
A command to hide from enemies
A request to sleep until morning
medium.explanation: The psalmist calls himself to awaken and praise God.
medium.q: What does “Awake up, my glory” mean in context?

answers: That the psalmist forgot his enemies
challenge.explanation: The psalmist responds to danger with steadfast worship.
challenge.q: What does readiness to sing despite danger demonstrate?

answers: It describes a change of location
It explains the structure of the cave
challenge.explanation: The repetition stresses his firmness and resolve to praise.
challenge.q: Why is the repetition of “my heart is fixed” significant?

answers: He rises before dawn to praise God
He tries to hide the dawn
challenge.explanation: He personally awakens early to sing and give praise.
challenge.q: How does “I myself will awake early” relate to the psalmist’s actions?

paragraphs.title: Praise Among the Nations and the Refrain

easy.explanation: He says, “I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people” and nations.
easy.q: Among whom does the psalmist promise to praise God?

answers: Only as far as the cave
Only as far as the sea
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thy mercy is great unto the heavens.”
easy.q: How great is God’s mercy according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The refrain says, “let thy glory be above all the earth.”
easy.q: What is to be above all the earth?

answers: Because God’s mercy and truth are great
medium.explanation: His praise is grounded in the greatness of God’s mercy and truth.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist want to praise God among the nations?

answers: The plea for refuge in the cave
The call for God to be exalted and His glory to fill the earth
The description of the enemies’ teeth
medium.explanation: The final verse repeats the call, “Be thou exalted, O God,” and the declaration of His glory.
medium.q: What is repeated at the end of the psalm?

medium.explanation: The image points to the vast heights of the heavens.
medium.q: What are “the clouds” in the expression “thy truth unto the clouds”?

answers: The focus moves from personal distress to worldwide praise
The earth is reduced to a cave
challenge.explanation: The psalmist moves from personal danger to praise among the nations and glory over all the earth.
challenge.q: What expansion takes place at the end of the psalm?

answers: The central importance of exalting God
Only the weakness of the enemies
challenge.explanation: The refrain places God’s exaltation at the center of the conclusion.
challenge.q: What does the repeated call “Be thou exalted, O God” emphasize?

answers: They are portrayed as extending from heaven over all the earth
They belong only to the enemies
challenge.explanation: Mercy reaches the heavens, truth reaches the clouds, and glory is declared over all the earth.
challenge.q: How are God’s mercy, truth, and glory connected?
